56453-the-egregious-english.title: The Egregious English
56453-the-egregious-english.creator: ANGUS McNEILL
56453-the-egregious-english.description: A book by ANGUS McNEILL. There is little that can be considered distinguishingly English which does not reflect this point of view. As an easy-going, entirely confident, imperturbable piece of arrogance, the Englishman has certainly no mammalian compeer. Even in the blackest of his troubles he perceives that he is great. "I shall muddle through," he says.

arxiv-1705-06846.title: A Predictive Account of Café Wall Illusions Using a Quantitative Model
arxiv-1705-06846.creator: Nasim Nematzadeh, David M.W. Powers
arxiv-1705-06846.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Nasim Nematzadeh, David M.W. Powers. This paper explores the tilt illusion effect in the Café Wall pattern using a classical Gaussian Receptive Field model. In this illusion, the mortar lines are misperceived as diverging or converging rather than horizontal. We examine the capability of a simple bioplausible filtering model to recognize different degrees of tilt in the Café Wall illusion based on different characteristics of the pattern.

arxiv-2102-02947.title: elementary amenable groups of cohomological dimension 3
arxiv-2102-02947.creator: Jonathan A. Hillman
arxiv-2102-02947.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jonathan A. Hillman. We show that torsion-free elementary amenable groups of Hirsch length ⩽ 3 \leqslant 3 are solvable, of derived length ⩽ 3 \leqslant 3 . This class includes all solvable groups of cohomological dimension 3 3 .

arxiv-2109-09549.title: On Some Properties of K K - type Block Matrices in the context of Complementarity Problem
arxiv-2109-09549.creator: A. Dutta, A. K. Das
arxiv-2109-09549.description: Abstract In this article we introduce K K -type block matrices which include two new classes of block matrices namely block triangular K K -matrices and hidden block triangular K K -matrices. We show that the solution of linear complementarity problem with K K -type block matrices can be obtained by solving a linear programming problem.

arxiv-2311-01571.title: On Preserving the Knowledge of Long Clinical Texts Journal: Heliyon
arxiv-2311-01571.creator: Mohammad Junayed Hasan, Suhra Noor, Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Khan
arxiv-2311-01571.description: Abstract Clinical texts, such as admission notes, discharge summaries, and progress notes, contain rich and valuable information that can be used for clinical decision-making. However, a severe bottleneck in using transformer encoders for processing clinical texts comes from the input length limit of these models: transformer-based encoders use fixed-length inputs.

arxiv-2311-09140.title: Rate-induced tipping in complex high-dimensional ecological networks DOI: www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.XXXXXXXXXX
arxiv-2311-09140.creator: Shirin Panahi, Younghae Do, Alan Hastings, Ying-Cheng Lai
arxiv-2311-09140.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shirin Panahi, Younghae Do, Alan Hastings, Ying-Cheng Lai. In an ecosystem, environmental changes as a result of natural and human processes can cause some key parameters of the system to change with time. Depending on how fast such a parameter changes, a tipping point can occur.

arxiv-2402-01529.title: Big data applications on small quantum computers
arxiv-2402-01529.creator: Boniface Yogendran, Daniel Charlton, Miriam Beddig, Ioannis Kolotouros, Petros Wallden
arxiv-2402-01529.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Boniface Yogendran, Daniel Charlton, Miriam Beddig, Ioannis Kolotouros, Petros Wallden. Current quantum hardware prohibits any direct use of large classical datasets. Coresets allow for a succinct description of these large datasets and their solution in a computational task is competitive with the solution on the original dataset. The method of combining coresets with small quantum computers to solve a given task that requires a large number of data points was first introduced by Harrow harrow2020small .

arxiv-2402-12947.title: Multigrid on unstructured meshes with regions of low quality cells
arxiv-2402-12947.creator: Yuxuan Chen, Garth N. Wells
arxiv-2402-12947.description: Abstract The convergence of multigrid methods degrades significantly if a small number of low quality cells are present in a finite element mesh, and this can be a barrier to the efficient and robust application of multigrid on complicated geometric domains.

arxiv-2404-14367.title: Preference Fine-Tuning of LLMs Should Leverage Suboptimal, On-Policy Data
arxiv-2404-14367.creator: Fahim Tajwar, Anikait Singh, Archit Sharma, Rafael Rafailov, Jeff Schneider, Tengyang Xie, Stefano Ermon, Chelsea Finn, Aviral Kumar
arxiv-2404-14367.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fahim Tajwar, Anikait Singh, Archit Sharma, Rafael Rafailov, Jeff Schneider, Tengyang Xie, Stefano Ermon, Chelsea Finn, Aviral Kumar. Learning from preference labels plays a crucial role in fine-tuning large language models. There are several distinct approaches for preference fine-tuning, including supervised learning, on-policy reinforcement learning (RL), and contrastive learning.

arxiv-2407-12920.title: A New Probe of μ \mu Hz Gravitational Waves with FRB Timing
arxiv-2407-12920.creator: Zhiyao Lu 1, Lian-Tao Wang 2, Huangyu Xiao 3,4
arxiv-2407-12920.description: Abstract We propose Fast Radio Burst (FRB) timing, which uses the precision measurements of the arrival time differences of repeated FRB signals along multiple sightlines, as a new probe of gravitational waves (GWs) around nHz to μ \mu Hz frequencies, with the highest frequency limited by FRB repeating period.

arxiv-2410-07544.title: Entanglement-Enhanced Neyman-Pearson Target Detection
arxiv-2410-07544.creator: William Ward, Abdulkarim Hariri, Zheshen Zhang
arxiv-2410-07544.description: Abstract Quantum illumination (QI) provides entanglement-enabled target-detection enhancement, despite operating in an entanglement-breaking environment. Existing experimental studies of QI have utilized a Bayesian approach, assuming that the target is equally likely to be present or absent before detection, to demonstrate an advantage over classical target detection.

arxiv-2412-07458.title: On the structure of open del Pezzo surfaces Thanks: This project was funded by the National Science Centre, and, grant number 2021/41/B/ST1/02062. For the purpose of Open Access, the authors have applied a CC-BY public copyright license to any Author Accepted Manuscript version arising from this sub
arxiv-2412-07458.creator: Karol Palka, Tomasz Pełka
arxiv-2412-07458.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Karol Palka, Tomasz Pełka. Let ( X ¯ , D ¯ ) (\overline{X},\overline{D}) be an open log del Pezzo surface of rank one, that is, X ¯ \overline{X} is a normal projective surface of Picard rank one, the boundary D ¯ \overline{D} is a reduced nonzero divisor on X ¯ \overline{X} , and − ( K X ¯ + D ¯ ) -(K_{\overline{X}}+\overline{D}) is ample.

arxiv-2501-08397.title: Predict Confidently, Predict Right: Abstention in Dynamic Graph Learning
arxiv-2501-08397.creator: Jayadratha Gayen, Himanshu Pal, Naresh Manwani, Charu Sharma
arxiv-2501-08397.description: Abstract Many real-world systems can be modeled as dynamic graphs, where nodes and edges evolve over time, requiring specialized models to capture their evolving dynamics in risk-sensitive applications effectively. Temporal graph neural networks (GNNs) are one such category of specialized models.

arxiv-2503-24014.title: Optimization of Layer Skipping and Frequency Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks under Latency Constraint
arxiv-2503-24014.creator: Minh David Thao Chan, Ruoyu Zhao *, Yukuan Jia, Ruiqing Mao, Sheng Zhou
arxiv-2503-24014.description: Abstract The energy consumption of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) is a critical factor in deploying deep learning models on resource-limited equipment such as mobile devices and autonomous vehicles. We propose an approach involving Proportional Layer Skipping (PLS) and Frequency Scaling (FS).

arxiv-2508-15295.title: Contribution of Globular Clusters to Diffuse Gamma-ray Emission from Galactic Plane
arxiv-2508-15295.creator: Jiayin He, Houdun Zeng, Yi Zhang, Xiaoyuan Huang, Qiang Yuan
arxiv-2508-15295.description: Abstract The diffuse Galactic γ \gamma -ray emission (DGE) provides a valuable probe for investigating the cosmic ray propagation and interactions within our Galactic environment. Recent observations have demonstrated systematic excesses of DGE compared with the conventional cosmic-ray propagation model predictions.

arxiv-2601-11217.title: Model-free policy gradient for discrete-time mean-field control
arxiv-2601-11217.creator: Matthieu Meunier, Huyên Pham, Christoph Reisinger
arxiv-2601-11217.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Matthieu Meunier, Huyên Pham, Christoph Reisinger. We study model-free policy learning for discrete-time mean-field control (MFC) problems with finite state space and compact action space. In contrast to the extensive literature on value-based methods for MFC, policy-based approaches remain largely unexplored due to the intrinsic dependence of transition kernels and rewards on the evolving population state distribution, which prevents the direct use of likelihood-ratio estimators of policy gradients from classical single-agent reinforcement learning.

arxiv-2602-11845.title: WorldTree: Towards 4D Dynamic Worlds from Monocular Video using Tree-Chains
arxiv-2602-11845.creator: Qisen Wang, Yifan Zhao, Jia Li
arxiv-2602-11845.description: Abstract Dynamic reconstruction has achieved remarkable progress, but there remain challenges in monocular input for more practical applications. The prevailing works attempt to construct efficient motion representations, but lack a unified spatiotemporal decomposition framework, suffering from either holistic temporal optimization or coupled hierarchical spatial composition .

pmc-11466415.title: Exploring the potential of structure-based deep learning approaches for T cell receptor design
pmc-11466415.creator: Helder V. Ribeiro-Filho, Gabriel E. Jara, João V. S. Guerra, Melyssa Cheung, Nathaniel R. Felbinger, José G. C. Pereira, Brian G. Pierce, Paulo S. Lopes-de-Oliveira, Nir Ben-Tal, Dina Schneidman, Nir Ben-Tal, Dina Schneidman, Nir Ben-Tal, Dina Schneidman, Nir Ben-Tal, Dina Schneidman
pmc-11466415.description: Deep learning methods, trained on the increasing set of available protein 3D structures and sequences, have substantially impacted the protein modeling and design field. These advancements have facilitated the creation of novel proteins, or the optimization of existing ones designed for specific functions, such as binding a target protein.

pmc-11495453.title: LncRNA TMPO-AS1 Promotes Triple-Negative Breast Cancer by Sponging miR-383-5p to Trigger the LDHA Axis
pmc-11495453.creator: Prerna Vats, Jai Singh, Sandeep K Srivastava, Ashok Kumar, Rajeev Nema
pmc-11495453.description: Background: Understanding the heterogeneous nature of breast cancer, including the role of LDHA expression regulation via non-coding RNAs in prognosis, is still unknown, highlighting the need for more research into its molecular roles and diagnostic approaches. Methods:The study utilized various computer tools to analyze the differences between LDHA in tissues and cancer cells. It used data from TIMER 2.

pmc-12565704.title: Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals and Male Infertility: Mechanisms, Risks, and Regulatory Challenges
pmc-12565704.creator: Sofoklis Stavros, Nikolaos Kathopoulis, Efthalia Moustakli, Anastasios Potiris, Ismini Anagnostaki, Spyridon Topis, Nefeli Arkouli, Konstantinos Louis, Charalampos Theofanakis, Themos Grigoriadis, Nikolaos Thomakos, Athanasios Zikopoulos, Yves Combarnous
pmc-12565704.description: Male reproductive health is increasingly threatened by endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), which interfere with hormonal homeostasis and reproductive physiology. Rising rates of male infertility have been linked to greater exposure to pollutants such as heavy metals, phthalates, pesticides, and bisphenol A.

pmc-12618240.title: Effectiveness of using a single-shade universal resin composite before internal bleaching: a 15-month follow-up case report
pmc-12618240.creator: Ryota Takaoka, Zhihao Zhai, Shion Morioka, Kenichi Nomura, Ami Aihara, Masahiro Nishimura
pmc-12618240.description: Single-shade universal resin composites allows light transmission from the surrounding tooth structure and light emission at a specific frequency, and it can reduce skill complexity, chair time, and inventory requirements. The present article aimed to demonstrate the aesthetic outcomes of restoring a tooth with a single-shade universal resin composite before internal bleaching.

pmc-12719554.title: Actin Takes the Steering Wheel: A New Mitotic Safeguard in the Early Embryo
pmc-12719554.creator: Yingqi Zhang, Shukai Zhu, Fangwei Wang
pmc-12719554.description: Early mammalian embryos undergo crucial cell divisions despite lacking fully functional centrosomes, presenting a paradox of how mitotic fidelity is maintained. This commentary discusses a seminal study by Hernandez et al. that overturns the microtubule-centric model of early embryonic mitosis by revealing 2 essential, complementary F-actin networks.

pmc-13499873.title: A Critical Systematic Review of Modelling Approaches and Methodologies used in Hyperlipidaemia Economic Evaluations
pmc-13499873.creator: Karl Vivoda, Harvey Koh, Tamrat Befekadu Abebe, Sheridan Rodda, Chris Bain, Zanfina Ademi

pmc-13538255.title: Establishment of a novel human nervous system tissue bank: University of Debrecen tissue bank—introduction and retrospective data analysis
pmc-13538255.creator: Viktor Bencs, Tibor Hortobágyi, Attila Csaba Nagy, Márk Kozák, Gábor Méhes, László Oláh, László Csiba
pmc-13538255.description: Human brain tissues obtained from autopsies, as well as muscle and nerve samples derived from biopsies, constitute indispensable resources for translational research investigating the pathomechanisms of neuropsychiatric disorders. In this study, we introduce the Nervous System Tissue Bank of University of Debrecen, which contains formalin-preserved and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) brain samples, as well as frozen nerve and muscle biopsy specimens.

pmc-13550499.title: Efficacy and Safety of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Followed by CDK4/6 Inhibitors Plus Endocrine Therapy in Patients With HR‐Positive, HER2‐Negative Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Single‐Centre Cohort Analysis
pmc-13550499.creator: Xiaopei Dong, Fan Li, Yang Yuan, Hua Song, Yingzhe Wang, Yi Hao, Yinping Dong, Tao Wang, Li Bian, Shaohua Zhang, Jianbin Li
pmc-13550499.description: BackgroundEndocrine therapy with CDK4/6 inhibitor has been the main treatment for HR+/HER2− breast cancer in the adjuvant setting; however, the data on the application in the neoadjuvant setting is limited. We compared neoadjuvant efficacy and safety of sequential chemotherapy‐CDK4/6 inhibitors with chemotherapy alone in HR+/HER2− breast cancer patients.

pmc-13659817.title: Engineering peroxygenases for pharmaceutical applications: recent advances and future perspectives
pmc-13659817.creator: Lilin Feng, Atul Kumar, Ulrich Schwaneberg, Marisa Sárria Pereira de Passos
pmc-13659817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Selective oxidation is a cornerstone process in pharmaceutical biosynthesis, as it enables the conversion of inert C–H bonds into valuable functional groups such as alcohols, ketones, epoxides, and carboxylic acids, which serve as important intermediates in drug synthesis. Peroxygenases, including unspecific peroxygenases and P450 peroxygenases, have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for enzymatic oxidation, with growing applications in metabolite synthesis, late-stage C–H functionalization, and the preparation of enantioenriched intermediates for pharmaceutical development.

pmc-7619357.title: Airway macrophage specific glycocalyx expression and remodeling following viral infection
pmc-7619357.creator: Ziyun Zhang, Iashia Z Nabi, Samie Dalgarno, H. Davies-Strickleton, Ilayda Akbulut, Tracy Hussell, Douglas P Dyer
